claims.text: High configurational entropy creates a single-phase structure in noble metal–based HEA nanoparticles.
A random distribution of noble-metal atoms leads to a broad, featureless valence band.
Diverse local electronic structures create multiple synergistic catalytic sites.
The diverse catalytic sites lower reaction barriers, including those for HER.
The five-component Ru-Rh-Pd-Ir-Pt nanoparticles have a homogeneous, atomically random configuration.
HER testing can be conducted in 0.05 M H2SO4 and 1.0 M KOH electrolytes.
The broad, featureless valence band is observable by hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
Entropy stabilization produces a uniform, disordered atomic distribution in the alloy nanoparticles.
The disordered atomic distribution creates a variety of local electronic structures or local densities of states.
The range of local electronic structures produces different adsorption environments that improve substrate binding.
The proposed adsorption environments lower kinetic barriers for catalytic reactions.
Monometallic Pt nanoparticles have a more uniform electronic structure than the HEA nanoparticles.
The HEA nanoparticles will have a broader valence band than monometallic Pt nanoparticles.
The HEA nanoparticles will have significantly higher HER turnover frequencies than monometallic Pt nanoparticles tested under identical conditions.
The HEA nanoparticles will require lower HER overpotentials than monometallic Pt nanoparticles.
The HEA nanoparticles will have greater operational stability than monometallic Pt nanoparticles.
The hypothesis should apply to HER under standard acidic and alkaline electrolytes when compositionally homogeneous nanoparticles are obtained.
Particle-size and surface-facet effects have not been fully separated from configurational-entropy and electronic-structure effects.
